claims.text: The target alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The applicable bulk specimens may contain approximately 1 wt.% oxygen or less.
The target specimen is high-purity, defect-free, and has a nominally perfect crystal structure.
The new method explicitly models temperature-dependent force constants and anharmonic phonon scattering.
The method isolates lattice vibrational transport from electronic heat conduction.
Severe intrinsic lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr produce local force-constant variations and anharmonic phonon interactions.
Local force-constant variations and anharmonic interactions control phonon mean free paths.
Calculating detailed vibrational spectra with anharmonic effects enables separate evaluation of phonon-scattering processes.
Explicit anharmonic calculations reduce reliance on a single Debye-temperature parameter.
Previous predictive models conflate electronic and lattice contributions.
Earlier Debye-based or analytical models have predictive errors of approximately 40% or more.
The new method will predict lattice thermal conductivity within approximately 30% of measured values.
Between 300 and 1200 K, the predicted lattice thermal conductivity will vary more gradually with temperature than predictions from earlier approaches.
Between 300 and 1200 K, lattice thermal conductivity will decline gradually as temperature increases.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
The model will correctly isolate the phonon contribution below 200 K.
The method will reduce predictive error by approximately 30% relative to earlier approaches.
The approach is applicable only to bulk, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr with minimal oxidation.
High defect densities, non-equilibrium microstructures, or greater oxygen contents introduce additional scattering mechanisms that can invalidate the model.
Thermal diffusivity and specific-heat measurements can be used to assess lattice thermal conductivity separately from electronic conductivity.

contradictions.description: The specimen is repeatedly described as defect-free and free of extrinsic scatterers while oxygen contamination up to approximately 1 wt.% is allowed; oxygen is an extrinsic species that can itself create disorder or scattering.
